About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you'll do

You'll own and evolve the technical systems that power P&T Business Operations — Jira architectures, data pipelines, dashboards, and integrations with enterprise platforms. You identify where operational capability could be stronger, scope those opportunities, and design and build solutions in collaboration with the Business Operations Manager. You approach problems with an AI-first mindset and make technical decisions with clarity about trade-offs.

  • Own and evolve the standardisation of Jira and other Kaluza data systems. Configure, extend, and redesign them to support increasingly complex business operations.

  • Build and maintain reliable data pipelines and dashboards that turn raw operations data into clear signals for decision-making. Explore where AI agents and autonomous systems can streamline operations.

  • Identify opportunities for new capabilities (better delivery planning data & tooling capabilities, improved management insights solutions, plugging into adjacent Kaluza products) and design and build solutions, aligned with the direction from the business operations manager who will lead the product & delivery enablement side of things

  • Connect and integrate internal products and platforms — Workday integrations, locally-built internal tools, and other solutions. Make recommendations on what to build, integrate, or take over — clearly articulating trade-offs, impact, and delivery path.

  • Anticipate security, compliance, and regulatory constraints upfront. Navigate Kaluza's systems to unblock delivery quickly.

  • Spot when something's off — in the data, in a process, or in a tool — and fix it before it becomes someone else's problem.

  • Iterate on our operational tooling continuously, testing new approaches early and sharing what you learn openly with the team.


What you'll bring

Ideally you'll have/be:

  • 3–5 years building and maintaining operational tooling — not just writing code, but owning what you ship.

  • Strong Jira expertise (including JQL) and Confluence; comfortable configuring them for complex portfolio structures.

  • Experience with APIs/integrations and data exchange, SQL + basic scripting, BI tools, AI tools and automation.

  • Experience building data pipelines or automated workflows with practical understanding of keeping them reliable at scale.

  • Confident in identifying improvements and implementing them independently. You break down ambiguous problems, scope solutions, and drive delivery without constant prompting. You don't wait to be told what's next.

  • Comfortable with data analysis, ambiguity, and working in scaling organisations where processes and systems need to grow as fast as the people using them.

  • You navigate Kaluza's systems to move fast. You share progress openly and communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.

What will set you apart:

  • You're the kind of person who spots a constraint, maps it back to its root cause, and builds a fix (or identifies where a temporary workaround is needed, whilst you work on a fix). You set a high bar for your own work and raise it over time, and you're not satisfied leaving a system in a worse state than you found it.

  • You work openly by default: you share progress, flag blockers early, and communicate what's working and what isn't without waiting to be asked. People across the organisation find it easy to understand what you're doing and why.

  • You're genuinely curious about new tools and approaches — especially AI — and you actively bring others along by sharing what you've tried, what landed, and what didn't. Learning in the open comes naturally to you.


Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.


Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app


Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

title: CDI - Manager Product Engineer - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Rémunération : 75 000€ à 85 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 8 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

LA MAISON JACQUEMUS Jacquemus a été fondée par Simon Porte Jacquemus en 2009 à Paris, en France. title: Clinical AI Research Lead
descriptionHtml:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi is building AI that works at the frontier of clinical practice. As we pursue medical device registration and expand our clinical trial portfolio and product portfolio, we need someone who can hold the full arc from regulatory strategy to research protocol to working prototypes and translate across all of them.

This role is designed for a rare profile: clinically trained, technically capable, and research-rigorous. You will own the innovation pipeline from problem identification through validated prototype, coordinate the company's clinical research programme, and serve as the internal bridge between product, regulation, and evidence. You will operate as a senior individual contributor with a small specialist team and broad cross-functional mandate.

 

What you’ll do

Research & Evidence Programme

  • Lead and support clinical trials and pilots adjacent to product development and regulation from protocol through analysis and dissemination

  • Design evaluations with research/publication-grade rigour: statistical power, confounder control, reproducible methodology

  • Provide analytical support company-wide - elevating ad hoc analysis to defensible evidence

Regulatory & Compliance Intelligence

  • Translate evolving UK and international medical device regulation into actionable product and development constraints

  • Generate and maintain technical documentation, clinical evaluation reports, and post-market surveillance artefacts - directly analytically supporting the regulatory team.

  • Partner with compliance to ensure regulatory soundness is built in, not bolted on, a strategic moat, not a checklist

  • Serve as the accessible regulatory resource for product, engineering, models and commercial teams: making regulation legible, usable and deeply embedded into all engineering practices.

  • This role is strategic support, and ownership of all product and regulatory adjacent research activities with a strong supporting team to drive progress and delivery.

Cross-functional AI & Research Support

  • Act as a senior research partner to product squads, commercial teams, and leadership, providing evidence, framing decisions, and raising analytical standards

  • Supporting commercial requests with tender applications etc…

 

What you'll need

Clinical

  • Qualified clinician with active understanding of clinical workflow, risk, and patient safety

  • Experience in medical device or clinical AI evaluation, including familiarity with MHRA, UKCA, and/or EU MDR frameworks

Research

  • Postgraduate research training in a relevant field (clinical informatics, AI/ML, health data science, or similar)

  • Demonstrated ability to design, execute, and disseminate clinical or applied research independently

  • Fluency in quantitative methods: statistical modelling, NLP evaluation, speech analytics, and performance benchmarking

  • Skills in implementation science and translational projects involving new technologies

Leadership & Communication

  • Strong written communication, capable of producing high-quality documentation for clinical, regulatory, and commercial audiences

  • Collaborative operator in a fast-moving environment; able to work across seniority levels and functions

  • Experience managing small teams or contractors; structured, outcome-oriented

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We offer 25 days of paid time off per year, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a €100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a €500 home office budget, a €700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to €7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

Heidi’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

Heidi is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all.

title: Clinical Training and Education Lead
descriptionHtml:
What is the job?

This is an opportunity to shape how our clinical teams learn, develop and perform as Montu continues to grow.

Sitting within the Learning and Development function, you will take ownership of the learning experience across our clinical teams. You will build structured, engaging and practical development programmes that give our people the knowledge, skills and confidence to deliver safe, consistent and patient-centred care.

You do not need to be a clinician or hold a professional healthcare registration. However, you will need to understand the realities of working in a clinical environment, including the importance of patient safety, clinical governance, regulatory compliance and quality.

Working closely with clinical subject-matter experts, operational leaders and the wider People team, you will turn complex standards, processes and clinical requirements into learning that people can understand, apply and embed in their everyday work.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is passionate about developing people, confident working with specialist stakeholders and comfortable building learning solutions in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

What You Will Own

Clinical Learning and Development

  • Own the learning and development plan for our clinical teams, ensuring it supports business priorities, service growth and workforce capability

  • Design and deliver structured onboarding, induction and ongoing development programmes for new and existing team members

  • Build clear learning pathways that support employees from joining the business through to continued development and career progression

  • Create engaging workshops, digital learning, practical resources and supporting materials for a range of clinical audiences

  • Conduct training needs analyses, skills audits and capability assessments to identify current and future development priorities

  • Deliver group workshops, virtual learning sessions and one-to-one coaching where required

  • Support the delivery and monitoring of mandatory training and continuing professional development requirements

Competency and Capability

  • Develop clear and practical competency frameworks in partnership with clinical subject-matter experts

  • Create consistent approaches to assessing knowledge, skills and competence across clinical teams

  • Work with managers to identify capability gaps and put appropriate development plans in place

  • Support leaders in embedding coaching, feedback and reflective practice within their teams

  • Ensure learning is transferred into day-to-day performance rather than ending when the training session finishes

Clinical Standards and Governance

  • Work closely with Clinical Governance, Quality, Safeguarding and operational leaders to ensure learning reflects current standards and requirements

  • Translate clinical policies, pathways, Standard Operating Procedures and regulatory requirements into clear and practical learning

  • Support the rollout of new clinical services, systems, technologies and ways of working through effective training and change support

  • Ensure relevant learning supports Care Quality Commission standards, patient safety requirements and internal governance expectations

  • Recognise where specialist clinical input or approval is required and work with the appropriate subject-matter expert

  • Maintain accurate learning, competency and compliance records across clinical teams

Learning Impact and Continuous Improvement

  • Establish clear measures of success for learning programmes and evaluate their impact on capability, performance and service quality

  • Use assessment outcomes, employee feedback, audit findings, quality data, incidents, complaints and patient feedback to identify learning priorities

  • Produce meaningful learning insights and reports to demonstrate progress, risks and areas for improvement

  • Regularly review and improve learning content to ensure it remains accurate, relevant and effective

  • Identify opportunities to improve how learning is delivered, recorded and embedded across the business

  • Champion a culture where learning, coaching, feedback and continuous improvement are part of everyday work

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Build credible and trusted relationships with clinical, operational and People leaders

  • Partner with subject-matter experts to create learning that is clinically accurate, engaging and appropriate for its audience

  • Coach and support managers to identify development needs and build capability within their teams

  • Balance learning priorities with operational requirements in a busy and fast-moving environment

  • Act as the Learning and Development lead for relevant clinical change and transformation projects

What do you need?

  • Strong experience within Learning and Development, workforce development, operational training or a similar role

  • A good understanding of clinical or healthcare environments, including patient safety, clinical governance, quality and regulatory requirements

  • Experience designing and delivering engaging learning programmes for specialist, operational or regulated teams

  • Strong learning design skills, with the ability to turn complex or technical information into clear and practical learning

  • Experience developing structured onboarding programmes, learning pathways or competency frameworks

  • Excellent facilitation, coaching and communication skills

  • The confidence to work with clinical specialists and senior stakeholders without needing to be the clinical expert in the room

  • Strong stakeholder-management skills and the ability to build credibility across different teams

  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving business

  • Strong project-management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver work through to completion

  • Experience using data, feedback and performance measures to evaluate learning and drive improvement

  • Experience supporting organisational change, service transformation or the implementation of new systems and processes

  • Confidence using learning management systems, digital learning tools and reporting platforms

  • A relevant Learning and Development, education or training qualification would be beneficial but is not essential

  • Professional registration with a healthcare body is a plus, but not required

 

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + 8 bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, private healthcare and more

  • Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams with support to grow your skills and impact

About Us

Montu is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

title: Cloud Engineer
descriptionHtml:

You will design, deploy, and maintain infrastructure on AWS and SecNumCloud-qualified cloud services so teams can work securely and reliably across both environments. This hands-on, high-ownership role sits at the intersection of aerospace and modern cloud engineering, with a strong focus on security, sovereignty, and compliance requirements.

You will work on-site in France and collaborate closely with engineering teams to translate their needs into resilient, secure, and well-documented infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, deploy, and operate cloud infrastructure on AWS and SecNumCloud-qualified cloud environments, including managed Kubernetes, compute, networking, storage, and managed database services.

  • Define and maintain a consistent architecture across AWS and SecNumCloud, including identity, networking, and secrets management, to keep environments comparable and portable where needed.

  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform) so all environments are reproducible and version-controlled.

  • Implement and maintain CI/CD pipelines that automate infrastructure and application builds, testing, and deployment.

  • Manage container platforms and orchestration, including Kubernetes cluster upgrades, networking, RBAC, and workload scheduling.

  • Set up and maintain observability (metrics, logging, alerting) to detect and resolve issues before they affect engineering or operations.

  • Enforce security and compliance best practices, including IAM policies, network segmentation, encryption at rest and in transit, key management, and vulnerability patching.

  • Support audits and compliance evidence collection for SecNumCloud and other applicable frameworks.

  • Define backup, retention, and disaster recovery strategies for critical data and services.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to understand their requirements and deliver reliable infrastructure solutions.

What we would love to see from you

  • 3+ years of experience in a cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or platform engineering role.

  • Deep hands-on experience with AWS or GCP, including compute, networking, storage, and managed database services.

  • Solid experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform, Terragrunt) and version control workflows.

  • Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or equivalent).

  • Strong understanding of networking concepts: VPCs, subnets, security groups, load balancers, DNS, and VPNs.

  • Working knowledge of containers and orchestration, ideally Kubernetes.

  • Experience with observability tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, or OpenTelemetry.

  • Willingness to learn sovereign and high-assurance cloud security requirements, and to apply them to cloud environments. Prior exposure is a plus but not required.

  • A security-first mindset with practical knowledge of IAM, secrets management, encryption, and compliance frameworks.

  • Fluent English. Working knowledge of French is not required but is considered an advantage.

  • Ability to work effectively in a multilingual team.

Nice to have

  • Experience in the aerospace, defense, or mission-critical systems domain.

  • Experience with multi-region or disaster recovery architectures.

  • Experience with hybrid or multi-cloud architectures across AWS and sovereign cloud providers.

  • AWS certifications (Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer - Professional) or equivalent.

  • Exposure to ISO 27001, FedRAMP, or other security certification environments.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:

title: Complaints Handler
descriptionHtml:
About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

Purpose of the role

Complaints are where things get real - the customer is already frustrated or in distress, the stakes are higher, and poor handling has direct regulatory consequences.

As a Complaints Handler, you'll own a caseload of customer complaints from acknowledgement through to final response. You'll investigate thoroughly, reach fair outcomes, and explain them clearly, all in line with DISP and Consumer Duty - and you'll take pride in getting it right for the customer first time.

You'll report to the Complaints Team Leader and work closely with teams across Claims, Fraud, Customer Support, and Sales to get to the right answer and fix the root cause.

Case Handling

  • Own and resolve a caseload of customer complaints following initial acknowledgement

  • Investigate each complaint thoroughly, analysing all the facts and related documentation

  • Gather the information you need from internal teams and external partners

  • Draft Final Response Letters that are clear, fair, and evidence a full investigation

  • Keep customers informed throughout and manage expectations along the way

  • Stay in control of your workload by actively monitoring and updating case management systems

Quality & Compliance

  • Keep complaints logged, acknowledged, and progressed within DISP timescales

  • Apply Consumer Duty and vulnerable customer standards consistently across every case

  • Escalate complex, sensitive, or high-risk cases to your Team Leader promptly

  • Support complaints reporting to management, senior leaders, QA assessors, and Compliance

Collaboration

  • Work with Claims, Fraud, Customer Support, and Sales to resolve complaints and address root causes

  • Contribute to feedback sessions, process improvement discussions, and complaint trend insight

What you will need to be successful

Essential

  • Proven experience handling complaints end to end within an FCA-regulated environment, ideally motor insurance.

  • Working knowledge of DISP and Consumer Duty as they apply to complaint handling.

  • Clear, concise written communication, and the emotional intelligence to handle difficult conversations well.

  • An analytical, organised approach - you can balance multiple priorities and deliver within SLAs.

  • You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to be an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.

Desirable

  • Experience of ShareDo or equivalent case management systems.

The Zego ways of working 🏡

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.

Here is what the last one looked like.

Benefits 🎁

💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.

🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.

📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build

🩺 Private medical insurance.

🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.

💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.

title: Customer Success Advisor
descriptionHtml:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We’re looking for a Customer Success Advisor

At iwoca, we value every customer and want them to have the best possible experience. Customer Success Advisors are at the heart of our Customer Success team, serving customers at all stages of their journey. Upon joining you’ll immediately become a key member of a highly motivated and energetic team.

The team

The Customer Success team are one of the main engine rooms of the business. They provide a quick, informative and dedicated service to iwoca's current and future customers. They are at the front line of all queries ensuring requests are met with a professional response.

This is a Leeds based team which continues to grow weekly providing incredible development opportunities in a supportive environment!

Want to get a deeper understanding of what life is like on the team? Read this blog from our Customer Success Mentor Conor.

The role

Your main responsibility will be delivering a positive customer journey. You’ll be engaging with business owners in a friendly manner and handle each query with expert care and efficiency. You'll be tasked with using your sales ability to convert inbound prospects and educating them on our services to meet their needs.

A typical day can include answering inbound calls to our main line, answering queries and requests as well as handling web chats and customer emails and helping businesses to complete their loan applications.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Ideally you'll have:

  • A passion for delighting customers and a real enthusiasm for helping SMEs. You’ll need to be able to build rapport with business owners quickly

  • Great time management and multitasking skills to be able to adapt to our customer’s needs

  • To be a self-starter taking ownership of your customers, whilst collaborating with your team to reach group targets

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and a professional manner

  • The ability to "think outside the box" and have the confidence to put forward ideas, often to other departments, to help us improve our processes

  • To be able to adapt to the growth of an ambitious company. You’ll take new products, customers groups and processes in your stride

  • We welcome people who are proactive, motivated and metrics-driven who have an ambitious and entrepreneurial spirit.

The salary

Our base salary range in Leeds is £28,000 - £29,000. We want to pay all of our employees fairly, so that’s why we regularly benchmark salaries based on market rates and to recognise your increasing value to our business.

For your first month in the role during training, there is a requirement to be in the office four times per week. This will then drop to once or twice per week upon completion of training. This is a Monday - Friday role working from 9 am to 6 pm.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

title: Cyber Exposure Management Expert (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
It all starts with the mission: NVISO is here to protect European society from potentially devastating cyber attacks. This means we offer cyber security services to private and governmental organizations to help them better prepare for, prevent, detect and respond to cyber security incidents. All of this is built on four fundamental values that define who we are: We are Proud, We Break Barriers, We Care and No BS!

Tasks

As Cyber Exposure Management Expert (m/w/d) located in Germany, you will be the technical lead for developing NVISO's Cyber Exposure offering. You will define how Vulnerability Management, Asset Management, hardening, Patch Management, reporting and remediation work together through clear processes and responsibilities, and guide the technical decisions that make the service work for our clients.

You will be the expert clients and colleagues turn to for the complete picture: which assets matter, where they are exposed, who needs to act and whether remediation has worked. You will design the processes, integrations and reporting that connect these questions, lead complex customer engagements and help other consultants deliver the service. You will advise on hardening and help clients establish ownership, remediation targets and a process that fits their IT operations.

You will also shape what we build next. Starting from our existing Vulnerability Management capabilities, you will develop the technical roadmap towards Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) and assess where Attack Surface analysis, exposure validation and Quantum Readiness belong in the offering. This gives you room to propose solutions, build prototypes and test them with clients before turning them into repeatable services.

Typical responsibilities include:

  • Defining the technical architecture and delivery approach for the Cyber Exposure offering, connecting Vulnerability Management, Asset Management, hardening, Patch Management, reporting and remediation, with clear roles and governance;
  • Leading technical delivery on customer engagements, advising on remediation and hardening, resolving design and integration problems and reviewing the quality of our work;
  • Linking vulnerability findings to asset inventories, CMDBs, cloud environments, business services and owners, and resolving gaps in coverage and data quality;
  • Designing remediation processes with owners, priorities, SLAs, escalation, risk acceptance and closure checks, aligned with Change Management and supported by ITSM, Patch Management and other remediation solutions;
  • Building reporting that shows clients their exposure and remediation progress, with clear priorities for technical teams and reliable measures of coverage, ageing, SLA performance and accepted risk for management;
  • Advising on secure configurations and hardening baselines for infrastructure and cloud environments, reducing unnecessary exposure and proposing compensating controls when patching is not immediately possible;
  • Keeping up with developments in Exposure Management and evaluating AI and agentic solutions through targeted pilots to improve existing approaches to prioritization, remediation guidance and reporting. You will test accuracy and usefulness, protect client data and define human oversight, including approval before AI recommendations trigger remediation actions;
  • Turning client needs into service packages, technical standards and delivery methods, coaching consultants and providing technical input for proposals and scoping;
  • Developing the service roadmap and evaluating new capabilities through pilots, including CTEM, Attack Surface analysis and cryptographic discovery, Crypto Agility and Post Quantum Cryptography migration planning. You will help decide which capabilities are ready to become services and what we need to deliver them well.

Requirements

  • You hold citizenship in one of the 32 NATO member states or the Austrian citizenship;
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent professional experience;
  • Strong practical experience in Vulnerability Management, including scanning platforms, prioritization based on asset criticality and exploitability, and remediation processes, with the ability to guide technical decisions on customer engagements;
  • Understanding of enterprise infrastructure, networking and cloud environments, with practical experience advising on secure configurations, hardening baselines and compensating controls;
  • Experience connecting security findings with asset inventories, CMDBs or Asset Management platforms, including ownership mapping and improving data quality;
  • Experience designing security dashboards and management reports that make priorities, progress and data limitations clear;
  • Experience designing remediation processes across security and IT teams, including ownership, SLAs, exceptions and Change Management. Familiarity with ITSM and remediation platforms is expected; scripting and API skills are an advantage;
  • Ability to design a solution across several tools and processes, explain the technical choices and guide colleagues through implementation. Experience developing a consulting service is an advantage;
  • Interest in developing CTEM and Quantum Readiness services and testing AI applications in security operations. Experience evaluating AI or agentic solutions is an advantage. Experience with Attack Surface analysis, Crypto Agility or Post Quantum Cryptography is welcome; you do not need to be an expert in every area on day one;
  • Fluent business English and professional fluency in the relevant local language(s).

Benefits

  • Working and learning from the best people in the European cyber security industry. We have multiple SANS Instructors working at NVISO, our staff has presented at popular hacking conferences (BlackHat, BruCON, OWASP, etc) and all of our technical staff can acquire deep technical security certifications (GSE, GXPN, GREM, GCFA, OSCP, etc);
  • Generous training budget of 10.000 EUR + 10 man days for attending lectures rolling over 2 years;
  • Base salary range (depending on experience and skillset): 70.000 EUR p.a. – 100.000 EUR p.a.;
  • Regular team-building and fun events;
  • Our commitment to coach and counsel you and help you grow; each employee receives a personal coach within the team, whose role is to ensure your well-being and helps you grow in your career!
  • Flexible working hours and home office possibilities (incl. working abroad weeks within the EU);
  • Business Bike Leasing;
  • BahnCard 50 1st class + public transfer ticket or EGYM WellPass;
  • 30 holidays;
  • Company Pension Scheme;
  • Cool offices in the center of Frankfurt, Munich and Vienna (with BBQ, kicker table, table tennis, playstations, etc.).

Disclaimer on the Use of AI Tools in the Application Process

Please be aware that the creation and submission of application documents (e.g. CV, cover letter, case studies, etc.) using AI-powered tools is only permitted to a limited extent.

Our expectations:

  • Application documents must authentically reflect your own qualifications, personality, and motivation.
  • The use of AI for supportive purposes (e.g. spell-checking, improving wording) is acceptable.
  • Fully generated application documents created by AI without personal adaptation or review are not permitted.
  • Under no circumstances may NVISO information, data, or documents be uploaded to or processed by external AI tools.

We reserve the right to exclude applications from the selection and interview process that are clearly created primarily or exclusively by AI and show no recognizable personal input.

The purpose of this policy is to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process and to obtain an authentic impression of our applicants.

title: Data Engineer, Finance
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Engelhart was founded in 2013 by BTG Pactual Group as a commodities trading company. Our business model is “asset light” and highly diversified – giving us the ability to adapt effectively and nimbly to changing market conditions. We have assembled successful multidisciplinary teams, leveraging advanced fundamental analysis with deep quantitative and weather research capabilities.  Our activities are underpinned by strong risk management practices and by powerful technology and operational excellence. We have exceptional teams with diverse global backgrounds and decades of experience, and are driven by a highly collaborative culture, across products and competencies.

In 2024, Engelhart acquired Trailstone, a global energy trading and technology company. The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. The acquisition also expanded Engelhart’s capabilities into physical natural gas across North America, a critical fuel to support the energy transition.

Our talented and experienced individuals work together according to its four company values: Performance, Agility, Collaboration, Entrepreneurship.

About the Role 

As a Data Engineer within Engelhart's Finance department, you will build and operate reliable data pipelines connecting the data warehouse and CTRM platform with brokers and Futures Commission Merchants (FCMs), margin and collateral processes, and the wider Finance technology stack. You will help automate manual Finance workflows into tested, monitored jobs, with robust reconciliations and controls that give stakeholders confidence in the completeness and accuracy of financial data. 

This will be a full-time role based in our London office and owning the following responsibilities: 

  • Build, operate and maintain data pipelines between the data warehouse, CTRM platform, brokers and FCMs, margin and collateral processes, and Finance systems. 
  • Integrate data from the Finance stack, including P&L and F+, SAP General Ledger, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, and bank statements. 
  • Automate manual Finance processes by developing reliable, tested and monitored jobs that can be operated and supported effectively. 
  • Implement reconciliations and data controls to identify missing or incomplete records, duplicates and breaks, and produce clear exception and break reporting. 
  • Ingest and process external files and feeds, including data received over SFTP and in formats such as CSV and XML. 
  • Investigate data and reconciliation issues, trace discrepancies through source systems and pipelines, and explain P&L or cash breaks to relevant Finance stakeholders. 
  • Develop and maintain serverless ETL solutions on AWS, using infrastructure as code and CI/CD practices to support consistent, controlled releases. 
  • Apply strong SQL and Python-based data processing to transform, validate and reconcile data accurately and efficiently. 
  • Work with Finance and technology stakeholders to understand requirements, improve existing workflows and deliver maintainable solutions with appropriate controls. 
  • Contribute to improving the reliability, observability and quality of Finance data flows as the business and its systems evolve. 

About You 

You will be a practical, analytical data engineer who combines strong software engineering skills with an understanding of Finance processes and controls. You can work with varied data sources, investigate discrepancies and explain the cause of a P&L or cash break clearly. You take ownership of the reliability of the jobs you build and look for opportunities to simplify and automate manual processes. 

As a result, we believe the following experiences and skills are essential for application: 

  • Strong Python development skills, including experience with Pandas and/or Polars, NumPy, and automated testing with pytest. 
  • Hands-on experience building AWS serverless ETL pipelines, using services such as Lambda, EventBridge, ECS/Fargate, DynamoDB, CloudWatch and S3. 
  • Experience with AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK), infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines. 
  • Experience building APIs using Python frameworks, preferably FastAPI. 
  • Strong SQL skills, including the ability to query, transform, validate and reconcile data. 
  • Experience ingesting external files and data feeds, including SFTP transfers and formats such as CSV and XML. 
  • Good understanding of Finance processes and data, with the analytical skills to investigate and clearly explain a P&L or cash break. 
  • A disciplined approach to testing, monitoring, reconciliation and control design, including checks for completeness, duplicates and exceptions. 
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail, with the ability to trace issues across systems and data pipelines. 
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with Finance and technical stakeholders. 

The following experience is not required, but highly desirable for this role: 

  • Experience using Kafka from Python. 
  • Experience integrating with SAP or treasury systems. 
  • Exposure to trading data, including positions and P&L. 
  • Familiarity with dbt and/or Airflow. 

What we offer 

  • Competitive compensation and participation in Engelhart’s discretionary bonus plan.  
  • 25 days of annual holiday entitlement, excluding UK public holidays. 
  • Robust benefits package such as medical, dental, life insurance, generous pension contribution, and supplemental benefits partially subsidised by the Company.   
  • Eligibility to receive external and internal training in accordance with our Training & Development Policy. 

We believe in inclusivity and are therefore dedicated to ensuring all employees – across gender identity, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, life experience, background and more – feel welcome and included in the company. We promote diversity because we believe it is essential to our ability to think holistically.

title: Data Scientist (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Make impact. Be human. Stay curious.

Who we are

We partner with leading organizations across industries to create scalable business impact by solving complex challenges through data, AI, and technology. Our team of 100+ data scientists, engineers, and change agents operates across Europe from offices in the Netherlands and Germany. Collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning are at the heart of our culture. Through topic communities, expert colleagues, and our internal academy, GAIN, you'll have plenty of opportunities to develop your skills in areas such as Agentic AI, Data Strategy, AI Product Development, and Technology Platforms, while helping clients achieve measurable results.

Join a team that loves learning, solving challenges together, and having fun along the way. Ready to join the ride?

Apply now! And let’s see where this journey takes us.

title: Datenschutzkoordinator / IT-Sicherheitskoordinator (w/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Als Datenschutz- und IT-Sicherheitskoordinator (w/m/d) koordinierst Du Datenschutz und Informationssicherheit bei Stackfuel in Deutschland und setzt sie gemeinsam mit unserem Compliance Team um. Du bist der Brückenkopf zur Datenschutzbeauftragten (DPO) und zum CISO in UK und sorgst dafür, dass DSGVO und Kundenanforderungen pragmatisch und effizient umgesetzt werden. So minimierst Du Risiken und ermöglichst den verantwortungsvollen Einsatz moderner Technologien.

Du kommst in einer entscheidenden Phase unserer Wachstumsgeschichte zu uns und verstehst Compliance als Enabler: Teams arbeiten schnell und sicher, Kund:innen vertrauen uns. Du berichtest an den Head of Product Compliance.

Schwerpunkte deiner Rolle

1. Datenschutzkoordination

  • Pflege von Verarbeitungsverzeichnis, TOM-Dokumentation, Löschkonzepten, Datenschutzhinweisen und Einwilligungsprozessen

  • Prüfung von Auftragsverarbeitungsverträgen sowie neuen Tools und Dienstleistern

  • Bearbeitung von Betroffenenanfragen, Vorbereitung von Datenschutz-Folgenabschätzungen

  • Behandlung von Datenschutz- und Sicherheitsvorfällen inkl. Meldeprozessen

2. Informationssicherheit

  • Koordination von Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung eines schlanken ISMS inkl. Risikoanalysen und Sicherheitsrichtlinien, abgestimmt mit dem DE- und UK-Compliance- und Security-Team

  • Steuerung technischer und organisatorischer Sicherheitsmaßnahmen mit IT-Abteilung und UK-Sicherheitsteam, inkl. Notfallvorsorge und Incident Response

3. Awareness & Schulung

  • Schulung und Sensibilisierung der Mitarbeitenden

4. Regulatorik & Lieferkette

  • Beobachtung und Bewertung von NIS-2, Cyber Resilience Act und AI Act

  • Lieferantenbewertung inkl. Sicherheitsfragebögen, Beantwortung von Kundenanforderungen und Unterstützung bei Audits

  • Regelmäßige Abstimmung mit DPO und CISO in UK

Das bringst Du mit

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium (z. B. (Wirtschafts-)Informatik) oder IT-Ausbildung mit Weiterbildung in Informationssicherheit

  • 3–5 Jahre Berufserfahrung in Datenschutz und IT-Sicherheit

  • Praktische Kenntnisse in DSGVO und BDSG (Verarbeitungsverzeichnis, Auftragsverarbeitung, DSFA, Betroffenenrechte)

  • Kenntnisse in Informationssicherheit und Risikomanagement (Risikoanalyse, Richtlinien, Incident Response)

  • Grundverständnis von IT-Infrastruktur, Cloud und Netzwerken; Kenntnisse in Identitäts- und Berechtigungsmanagement (MFA, SSO), Endpoint-Schutz, Backup sowie Patch- und Schwachstellenmanagement

  • Kommunikationsstärke, didaktisches Geschick (auch gegenüber Nicht-Techniker:innen) und Durchsetzungsvermögen

  • Strukturierte, sorgfältige Arbeitsweise mit Dokumentationsdisziplin, Pragmatismus, Priorisierungsfähigkeit, Integrität und Diskretion

  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch (mind. C1)

  • Zertifizierung als Datenschutzbeauftragte/r bzw. -koordinator/in oder Bereitschaft, diese im ersten Jahr zu erwerben; Bereitschaft zur Weiterbildung

Von Vorteil:

  • Erfahrung im Aufbau oder in der Weiterentwicklung eines ISMS; Kenntnis von ISO 27001 oder BSI IT-Grundschutz und eine entsprechende Zertifizierung (oder Bereitschaft dazu)

  • Kenntnisse zu NIS-2, Cyber Resilience Act und AI Act

  • Erfahrung mit Kundenaudits und Lieferantenbewertungen

  • Kenntnisse in Logging und Monitoring sowie Erfahrung mit Cloud-Umgebungen

Das bieten wir Dir

 

Arbeitskultur
Dich erwartet eine lösungsorientierte und datengetriebene Arbeitsweise, eine offene Feedbackkultur sowie ein starker Teamspirit. Zwei vom gesamten StackFuel-Team gewählte Trustees unterstützen Dich bei Fragen und Anliegen als neutrale, vertrauliche Anlaufstelle.

Ownership
Übernehme ab dem ersten Tag Verantwortung, bringe Deine eigenen Ideen aktiv ein, gestalte Prozesse nachhaltig und präge unsere Abläufe maßgeblich mit.

Hybrides Arbeiten
Wir arbeiten in einem hybriden Modell und sind üblicherweise 3 Tage pro Woche vor Ort in unserem Office in Berlin.

Workation
Bis zu 10 Tage pro Jahr kannst Du von überall aus der EU, dem EWR und der Türkei arbeiten.

Raum für Austausch
Regelmäßiger Austausch im Team, saisonale Feiern und eine immer gut gefüllte Küche sorgen für ein lebendiges Miteinander.

Weiterentwicklung
Absolviere unsere Online-Trainings, um Deine fachlichen Fähigkeiten auszubauen und Dich zur Expert:in für Daten und KI zu entwickeln.

title: Defense Success Manager, France
descriptionHtml:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

  • Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

  • Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

  • Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules.

  • Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion

  • Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.


Nice to have

  • Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs.

  • Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

  • Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

Security & Compliance criteria

title: Developer Experience Engineer - AI SDLC
descriptionHtml:
We Are Sparta

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

The role

You lead how Sparta builds software in the AI era. You own our AI-native software development lifecycle: the development agents engineers work alongside, the CI/CD that ships their code, and the testing strategy that lets us move fast without breaking trading workflows.

AI has changed how code gets written, reviewed, and tested, and the tooling has not caught up. Your job is to make an engineer with Claude Code, a good harness and a fast pipeline several times more effective, and to prove it with data, not anecdotes.

What you will do

  • Own the AI development toolchain. Set up and evolve Claude Code and other development agents across engineering: shared skills, MCP servers, repo context, and guardrails, so agents work well in our codebase out of the box.

  • Build agents into the lifecycle. Automate the work around the code: AI-assisted code review, test generation, dependency upgrades, migrations and incident triage, with humans in the loop where it matters.

  • Make CI/CD fast and boring. Own build, test and release pipelines across the Nx monorepo: caching, affected-only builds, preview environments and safe, frequent deploys to AWS.

  • Build the guardrails for everyone who builds. Anyone can build now, including product, design, data and domain experts working with agents. Create the tooling that makes it safe for them to contribute code: automated quality gates, code ownership and review rules, preview environments, policy checks and agent evals in the pipeline, so good changes ship fast and risky ones are caught early. Testing strategy sits inside this: define what we test at each level and make the right tests cheap to write.

  • Keep it secure. Secrets, permissions and sandboxing for agents that read code and run commands, and supply-chain checks in the pipeline.

  • Raise the bar for everyone. Run enablement, write the playbooks, pair with teams and turn good practice from one team into the default for all of engineering.

What you bring

  • Extensive experience as a hands-on software engineer, with recent focus on developer experience, platform or build and release engineering.

  • You have rolled out AI coding tools to a team and made them stick: you know where agents help, where they fail and how to set them up for a real codebase.

  • You lead without needing authority: you treat engineers as customers, listen first, and win adoption with tools people want to use.

Nice to have

  • Built Claude Code skills, plugins or MCP servers, or extended another agent harness.

  • Deep CI/CD experience: you have designed pipelines for a monorepo, cut build and test times, and run safe, frequent releases.

  • Infrastructure as code and container platforms.

  • Experience defining or running engineering metrics.

Our stack for this team

Claude Ecosystem · Nx monorepo · GitHub · AWS · TypeScript · Python · Kotlin

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.
